title: Alterac Mountains
body: These cold peaks between Lordaeron and the Hillsbrad foothills were once a proud human kingdom. Alterac began as a city-state of the old Arathorian empire, but in the Second War its king, Aiden Perenolde, secretly struck a bargain with Orgrim Doomhammer and let the Horde march through his mountain passes unopposed. When the treason came to light, King Terenas marched into Alterac, declared martial law and deposed him. The kingdom never recovered. Today the Crushridge ogres squat in the ruined capital, while the Syndicate, a gang of thieves led by Alterac's disgraced nobles under Aliden Perenolde, holds Strahnbrad and the Uplands and dreams of taking the land back. Darker masters steer the Syndicate in secret. On the shore of Lordamere Lake lies the crater left by Dalaran, its wizards still patrolling the ruins, and hidden in the eastern hills the assassins of Ravenholdt wage their own quiet war on the Syndicate. Yetis haunt the high caves, and both Southshore and Tarren Mill send agents north into the snow.

title: Sofera's Naze and Corrahn's Dagger
body: North and west of Tarren Mill, where the foothills climb into the mountains, the Syndicate keeps two rough camps at Sofera's Naze and Corrahn's Dagger. Footpads and thieves loiter about the tents, and a few drunkards among them sing the praises of Southshore stout. Papers left on the camp tables are worth reading: one lists black masks, paralytic poison, stolen guard uniforms and rations for twenty men, all for an important mission against Southshore, signed by a Baron V. Another, left with a dying henchman named Valik, orders him to guard a slave until it can be moved north, out of sight. Southshore's new magistrate blames the Syndicate for his predecessor's murder, and these camps are where he looked first.

title: Strahnbrad
body: Strahnbrad was a mountain village of Lordaeron, defended in the Third War by Uther and Prince Arthas when Blackrock orcs raided it for slaves to sacrifice. Many of its people died, and the rest are long gone. The Syndicate now uses the town as its main base, and spies, wizards and the mysterious shadow mages of the Argus Wake walk its streets. Southshore's magistrate believes the gang's noble leaders hide here among common cutthroats, betrayed only by the signet rings of Alterac they still wear. The gang keeps prisoners here too: the orc Gol'dir was held in chains in a locked room, while the jailor Borhuin kept the key.

title: The Headland
body: The Headland is a rugged spur of the mountains above the Hillsbrad foothills, riddled with caves where ferocious yetis den. In the Foothill Caverns here, the wizard Helcular raised two ceremonial pyres, the Flame of Azel and the Flame of Veraz, for the ritual that was meant to make him a lich, and their fires still burn. A mob from Southshore killed him before the work was done, and the yetis took over his lair. Mountain lions prowl the cliffs, and dwarves of the Stormpike clan keep a camp here on the road north.

title: Growless Cave
body: High in the mountains above the Foothill Caverns, Growless Cave is a den of mountain yetis and the giants of their kind. Helcular built the third of his pyres here, the Flame of Uzel, and its fire still burns in the cold. Hunters who know the old lore use it as a lure: meat burned on the flame draws Frostmaw, an elusive yeti whose white coat hides him against the snow. During the Feast of Winter Veil the cave gains a stranger tenant, a creature called the Abominable Greench, who steals holiday treats and leaves those who cross him frozen into snowmen.

title: Ruins of Alterac
body: The capital of Alterac was emptied when the kingdom fell, and after the Third War its deserted halls were claimed by the Crushridge ogres. Their warlord Mug'thol rules from the ruins of the old palace, with warmongers, maulers and ogre mages filling the broken streets. Among them wanders Grel'borg the Miser, a greedy ogre mage who spends his days digging through the rubble for baubles; rumor says he found the Perenolde Tiara, an heirloom of the old royal family crafted by Ironforge jewelers and set with emeralds. Wrecked meat wagons near the northern gate hint that the undead once tried to storm the place.

title: Crushridge Hold
body: Beside the ruined capital, the Crushridge ogres have dug an ogre mound of their own into the mountains. Crushridge Hold is their stronghold, crowded with ogres and brutes, and their camps spill out into Slaughter Hollow and along the old road at Gallows' Corner, where they prowl around a ruined scout tower. The slopes here are rich in mithril and truesilver, and at least one bold trader in engineering supplies has set up shop in Slaughter Hollow. Southshore pays bounties on ogre knucklebones, fearing that if the Crushridge grow comfortable here they will move down into the foothills next.

title: The Uplands
body: North of Strahnbrad lie the Uplands, the farmlands that once fed the kingdom of Alterac. Today this is where the Syndicate is strongest. Sentries and saboteurs guard its camps, the shadow mages of the Argus Wake come and go, and Baron Vardus, a cold-hearted Alterac noble wanted by both Southshore and the Forsaken, has been seen among them. Not every house here belongs to a thief. Beside the lake lives Nancy Vishas, whose husband serves the Scarlet Crusade as an interrogator, and who waits anxiously at home whenever his work at the Monastery keeps him late.

title: Dandred's Fold
body: On the western edge of the Uplands, a farm and manor house look down on a small harbor on Lordamere Lake, near the Misty Shore. This is Dandred's Fold, the residence of Lord Aliden Perenolde, who styles himself lord of these lands and runs the Syndicate from here. Its grounds are guarded by the gang's assassins and enforcers. Within the manor, Perenolde keeps his mistress Elysa, and he meets here with Nagaz of the Argus Wake, the hidden power whose hand guides the Syndicate's ambitions. Snapping turtles crawl along the misty lakeshore below.

title: Lordamere Internment Camp
body: On a hill above the crater of Dalaran stands the Lordamere Internment Camp, the only prison camp in the mountains, held by Dalaran's shield guards and theurgists under Warden Belamoore. Its newest inmates are four Forsaken who deserted the Undercity after breaking into a secure vault and stealing four artifacts, pieces of bloodstone the royal apothecaries needed for their studies. The thieves fled to Dalaran, and the wizards quarantined them here. The Dark Lady wants her property returned and the deserters punished.

title: Dalaran Crater
body: Dalaran, city of the Kirin Tor, was laid waste in the Third War when the Burning Legion's Archimonde was summoned before its walls. The wizards later raised a vast violet dome over the heart of their ruins and rebuilt behind it, and in time they lifted their reborn city whole into the skies of Northrend. All that remains on the shore of Lordamere Lake is a gaping crater beneath a dome now faded nearly to nothing, ringed by broken walls. Some mages stayed behind. Summoners and their bound earth elementals still patrol the ruined outskirts, workers labor in the rubble, and a few archmages keep watch over what is left.

title: Ravenholdt Manor
body: Hidden in the eastern hills above Hillsbrad, at the end of a winding mountain path northwest of Durnholde, stands Ravenholdt Manor, seat of the Assassin's League. Outsiders are not welcome. The guards greet strangers with a warning to watch their backs, and the assassins on the grounds are quicker still to show their contempt. Within, Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over a guild of thieves and killers that admits only the most gifted. The manor has its own poison seller, a specialist engineer, a garden kept by a landscape architect, and a training arena that is the domain of the orc Master Kang. Its long war is with the Syndicate.

title: Chillwind Point
body: On the far eastern edge of the mountains, beside the river that runs north past Tarren Mill, a small rise is crowned by the ruins of an ancient troll site. Chill winds sweep down through a nearby ravine from the Plaguelands to the north, and give the point its name. Here the jungle troll hermit Bath'rah the Windwatcher keeps his camp and his cauldron, watching the ruins for a great elemental lord of the winds he calls Cyclonian. A red drake, Narillasanz, is sometimes seen in these eastern heights.

title: Lord Aliden Perenolde
body: Aliden is the eldest son of Aiden Perenolde, the king who sold out the Alliance to the Horde. For two years after the Second War he tried to wash that stain from the family name, rising through the ranks at Durnholde under his mentor Aedelas Blackmoore. Then he left Blackmoore's service for the mountains of Alterac and founded the Syndicate. From his manor at Dandred's Fold he styles himself lord of the land, and he means to enslave the orcs who stand against him, just as his father and Blackmoore once planned. Nagaz of the Argus Wake keeps close at his side, and his young mistress Elysa wore a pendant the Warchief himself wanted back.

title: Mug'thol
body: Mug'thol is warlord of the Crushridge ogres and master of the ruined city of Alterac. He rules from what is left of the old palace, with his loyal lieutenants Targ, Muckrake and Glommus at his side and the greedy ogre mage Grel'borg the Miser among his followers. He was not always his own master. The Banshee Queen once bound him to her will through a banshee's possession and sent him into Alterac after a relic, the Crown of Will. He put the crown on, and it set him free. The Forsaken have not forgiven the insult, and Southshore fears his ogres will push down into the foothills next.

title: Gol'dir
body: Gol'dir led the band of orc warriors the Warchief sent from Durotar to look into the Syndicate and to recover a small trinket Thrall wanted back. The humans overwhelmed them at Durnholde, and Gol'dir was carried off and moved from place to place until the Syndicate chained him in Strahnbrad. His captors set him to hauling burdens and digging, and the jailor Borhuin kept the key to his chains. There Aliden Perenolde himself came to boast of his plans to enslave the orcs, bringing along a mistress who wore the very pendant the Warchief sought. Gol'dir counts his own suffering as unimportant: what matters is that his people learn what he heard.

title: Baron Vardus
body: Baron Vardus is a noble of fallen Alterac, known for his cold heart and brutal methods, and a high-ranking member of the Syndicate. A supply list for a raid on Southshore bears the signature of a Baron V., the gang's quartermaster, and a contract for the murder of Magistrate Henry Maleb, sealed in red wax with a distinctive signet, was signed with his name. That was enough for Southshore to demand his head. The Forsaken want him dead as well, for crimes against them, and High Executor Darthalia of Tarren Mill has posted a bounty. He was last seen in the Uplands.

title: Nagaz
body: Nagaz is a hierophant of the Argus Wake, the shadowy circle that quietly steers the Syndicate, and the hand of his master's will in Alterac. He keeps close to Lord Perenolde at Dandred's Fold. In a letter to that master, written in one of the Wake's most obscure ciphers and signed in the name of Sargeras, he mocked the Alterac nobles for a bargain they would regret. He meant to steer them toward Stromgarde and so win the Wake a nation of its own, from which to prepare the way for the Third Host of the Burning Legion. Southshore wants his head, though its magistrate fears Nagaz is only a servant and the Wake runs far deeper.

title: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt
body: Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is master of the Assassin's League, the order of thieves and killers that gathers at Ravenholdt Manor. After the Third War he took up the hunt for the Syndicate in these mountains, and the League has fought the gang ever since. With far fewer blades than their enemy has members, the League pays skilled rogues to shame Syndicate members by stealing their emblems. His grand master, Fahrad, trains the guild's rogues and sends anyone else away with a threat. Jorach greets those he needs with open arms and rewards loyal service generously, but keeps his own secrets close: the contents of a sealed azure bag he once lost were, he said, a private matter.

title: Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver
body: Ansirem Runeweaver is a senior archmage of the Kirin Tor, and by the Third War sat on the Council of Six. When Antonidas fell he fought outside the walls of Dalaran against Arthas and the Scourge while Kel'Thuzad called down Archimonde. Now that Dalaran has risen to Northrend, he is among the few mages who stayed at the crater. His learning ranges far: years ago he wrote a tome on the legends of the Gurubashi Empire, and he cannot resist a magical puzzle. His willful daughter Catelyn gave up the mage's life and ran off to Booty Bay to become a pirate.

title: Archmage Cedric
body: Archmage Cedric is an agent of the Violet Eye, the order the Kirin Tor assigned to watch over Karazhan and Medivh. He waits among the ruins at the edge of Dalaran Crater, unmoved by the desolation around him and certain that Dalaran is as powerful as ever. When Archmage Alturus sent word of a demonic presence stirring in the sealed tower, it was Cedric who read the report and sent it on to Shattrath, to Khadgar, the one man still living who was thought able to open Karazhan again. Those who help the Violet Eye may earn its trust, and its badge.

title: Bath'rah the Windwatcher
body: Bath'rah is a jungle troll shaman and weaponcrafter who has taken up a hermit's life at the troll ruins of Chillwind Point. For ages, he says, he has watched the site, waiting for a champion able to bring down Cyclonian, the lord of the winds who can be called there. Those who gather what his summoning needs may face the elemental, and from its whirlwind heart Bath'rah will forge a weapon. Lately the spirits of the place have turned against him, and he has sought a spirit totem, strengthened with troll voodoo, to guard his sleep.

title: Nancy Vishas
body: Nancy Vishas lives in a house in the Uplands near Lake Lordamere, where she waits anxiously for her husband to come home from his work at the Monastery. Her husband is the Scarlet Crusade's Interrogator Vishas, and his work is torture. One of his victims, the Forsaken Vorrel Sengutz, was held and tormented for weeks, and saw his own wedding ring taken and given to Nancy. Vorrel's dying wish was that she be found and slain, and the ring returned to his widow Monika in Tarren Mill. An old man called Grandpa Vishas shares the house and has no patience for her fretting.

title: The Bloodstone Thieves
body: Some months ago four Forsaken deserted the Undercity, and before they fled they broke into a secure vault and stole four artifacts the royal apothecaries needed for their studies. They ran to Dalaran, and the wizards locked them away in the Lordamere Internment Camp. Magus Wordeen Voidglare, who had come to Tarren Mill only to research, found himself charged with getting the artifacts back for the Dark Lady and seeing the deserters, Kegan Darkmar among them, brought to justice. The Magus has his own interests too. He has the patrols of summoners and elemental slaves around Dalaran thinned so that the ruins can be searched for magical treasures, and Keeper Bel'varil, who serves him, collects the stone tokens the wizards use to command their elementals, and the binding bracers set on the elementals themselves, for the Magus to study.
